descriptionChirho: A female of any species (human or animal), used to denote sex/gender distinction. All three clusters represent the same noun נְקֵבָה with different prepositional and conjunctional framing ('female,' 'and female,' 'and for the female'). Cross-lingual evidence is unanimous: Arabic أُنْثَى (untha, female), Swahili 'jike' (female animal) and 'mwanamke' (woman), Hindi मादा (mada, female) and स्त्री (stri, woman), Korean 암컷 (amkeot, female) and 여자 (yeoja, woman), Spanish 'hembra' (female) and 'mujer' (woman). Used in creation accounts (Gen 1:27, 5:2, 6:19, 7:3,9,16) and Levitical regulations (Lev 3:1,6, 4:28,32, 5:6, 12:5,7, 27:4-7; Num 5:3, 31:15; Deut 4:16).
